ashtapada.evidence: Read all main-rule text and inspected original rule/board pages. Modern reconstruction published as a six-page A4 Games Company printable booklet; PDF pages 1–3 contain the introduction and all 27 numbered rules, while pages 4–6 are printable board/counters/casting sticks retained in the unchanged original. Not evidence of uniquely authentic ancient rules. Four sticks/cowries score 1–4, with all backs scoring 8; enter on 1, repeat throws until 2/3, use a player-specific spiral route, capture/re-enter, use safe marked squares/twins, exact entry to the keep and bear off on 1. The booklet has an inconsistent optional 1–5 spinner/strategy paragraph, and uses twins/keep terminology without a full glossary; those ambiguities are preserved rather than silently repaired. Use the casting-stick rules and original route diagram when consulting this reconstruction. Summary not audited; reconstruction differences alone are not treated as errors.

mangala.evidence: Original-language Turkish modern 48-stone/2×6 Mangala rules from Ata Sporları Federasyonu, supported by Viranşehir district education authority’s November 2024 tournament PDF pages 3–5 (Mangala section only). Federation page supplies four-seed setup and majority victory; tournament rules explicitly supply skipping the opponent’s treasury, single-stone movement, 2/4/6/etc. captures, empty-own/opposite capture and end sweep awarded to the player whose row emptied. Directions are described inconsistently as right/left in the federation prose; tournament PDF explicitly says counterclockwise toward the own treasury. This is modern Turkish Mangala, not the earlier Bedouin/Greek/historic five-seed regional variants. Original HTML/PDF retained; selected text remains Turkish without an invented translation; source-specific match/touch/clock rules are preserved. No summary audit.

mehen.evidence: Six-page Tabletopia-hosted English Mehen reference with simple and complex playable modern reconstructions; full text read. It explicitly says original ancient rules cannot be recovered. Simple version: six pawns/lion per player, tail-to-head race, throwing-stick values, accumulated throws, capture/re-entry, stacking and lion rules, all pawns safe at the head wins. Complex version adds stored ones, return journey, faster lions and capture-count ending; its introductory all-pawns statement and numbered first-returning-pawn lion trigger disagree, so consult that variant critically. Dice face values are diagrammatic on page 3; use original PDF. Awkward English and speculative historical claims are not certified by recovery. These are named reconstructions, not authenticated ancient rules or a complete summary audit.

royal-game-of-ur.evidence: Read all main-rule text and inspected original rule/board pages. J. Paul Getty Trust museum activity packet, PDF pages 13–15 only; the unchanged original contains other games. This is Getty’s playable seven-piece reconstruction adapted from Irving Finkel’s Games, not a surviving ancient rulebook or a claim that every modern variant agrees. Uses a six-sided die rerolled on 5/6, colored-square extra throws, exact exit, and doubled pieces that move together and are safe. That doubling rule differs from the current summary’s no-stacking variant. Board/path diagrams must be consulted in the original PDF. Summary not audited; reconstruction differences alone are not treated as errors.
